title: MOE Huayu Enrichment Scholarship
deadline_central_display: No single date - the application period is set by each authorized overseas office, usually January or February each year
deadline_note: The application period is announced by each authorized overseas office, usually January or February each year. You must separately apply to a Chinese language center and supply proof of application with your scholarship application. The results are announced no later than the first day of March every year and successful applicants enrol between July and August.
application_cycle: Annual; application period announced by each authorized overseas office, usually January or February, with results by 1 March and enrolment between July and August
status_note: The current cycle's application period (usually January or February) has passed; the next cycle is expected to open around January 2027.
benefits: Study periods from a 2-month summer course to a 3-, 6-, 9-month or one-year course
Choice of a government-designated Chinese language center at a university or college in Taiwan
Places at universities and colleges that receive no more than half of their quota through authorized overseas offices
eligibility: Applicants must have attained the age of eighteen years
Applicants must possess a senior high school diploma or above
Applicants must be of good physical and mental health
Applicants must be of good moral character
Applicants with a good academic record and an interest in Mandarin Chinese
requirements: Applicants who currently have full-time employment in the public service sector are not eligible
Applicants must not be engaged in full-time work in the private sector
Applicants must not currently be enrolled in a program of study at an educational institution in Taiwan
Applicants must not be exchange students sent by an educational institution in a foreign country
Applicants who have previously applied for the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship three times or more are not eligible
Apply separately to a Chinese language center and supply proof of application with the scholarship application
coverage: A monthly stipend of 28,000 NTD for the duration of the course
application_method: Submit an application to an authorized overseas office during the period announced by that office
application_route: Apply through an authorized overseas office during the stated application period, having separately applied to and been accepted by a Chinese language center at a university or college in Taiwan.
duration: 2-month summer course, or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course
description: The Ministry of Education Huayu Enrichment Scholarship provides foreign students with opportunities to study Mandarin Chinese at government-designated centers in Taiwan.

verification.notes: Stipend, purpose and both eligibility lists were read directly from the Ministry of Education Taiwan scholarship page. The page does not set a single closing date - the application period is announced by each authorized overseas office, usually January or February each year, with results announced no later than 1 March and successful applicants enrolling between July and August. Whether the stipend is intended to cover tuition or living costs is not stated on the page.

applicant_utility: This is Taiwan's Mandarin-language scholarship, not a degree scholarship: it pays a monthly stipend of NT$28,000 while you attend a designated Chinese language center, with course lengths that range from a two-month summer course to a full year. A practical sequence to follow - apply separately to a Chinese language center first, because you must supply proof of that application with your scholarship application to the authorized overseas office. Give yourself a realistic timeline: applications usually run January or February, results are announced by 1 March, and successful applicants enrol between July and August. Check the eligibility list carefully before you invest time in it. Anyone in full-time public sector work is excluded, full-time private sector workers are excluded, current students at Taiwanese institutions are excluded, and if you have applied three times before you are no longer eligible.

title: Taiwan International Graduate Program Scholarship
deadline_central_display: 1 November to 1 February each year (GMT+8); the most recent application period closed 1 February 2026
deadline_note: The application period is 1 November to 1 February (GMT+8). Only one PhD programme may be selected. The most recent cycle closed 1 February 2026; the dates and result announcements for the next cycle are typically announced in November and the middle of March.
application_cycle: Annual application period from 1 November to 1 February (GMT+8)
status_note: The most recent cycle closed on 1 February 2026; the next intake opens 1 November.
tuition_coverage_note: Academia Sinica subsidises the difference between international tuition fees and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years. International students still pay the domestic tuition rate of about NT$28,000 to 31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and about NT$16,000 to 20,000 for the rest of their study.
benefits: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 plus NT$6,000) for the first year
The stipend is extended for one more year for students who perform well
Academia Sinica subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years
After the first year, the stipend is dependent on the individual thesis advisor
eligibility: International students who satisfy both the general and the programme-specific admission requirements
Applicants must not already hold the degree level applied for
There is no application fee, regardless of the applicant's nationality
requirements: Apply online between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8)
Select only one TIGP programme (only one PhD programme is permitted)
Choose a thesis advisor before the end of the first year; students may instead join laboratories outside their affiliated programme with individual approval
Abide by the Academic Integrity Statement - plagiarism and ghostwriting result in disqualification and withdrawal of the degree
If you pass the preliminary evaluation, send both the paper original and a scanned copy of the application documents by post or courier
coverage: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable one further year for students who perform well
Subsidy of the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years
Domestic-rate tuition fees remain payable by the student
application_method: Apply online at http://tigp.apps.sinica.edu.tw/index.php between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8)
Provide referee details in the online application; recommenders receive portal instructions after 1 March and must submit online before 1 April
After preliminary evaluation, send paper originals and scanned copies of documents by post or courier
application_route: Online application through the TIGP application portal, with referee details entered online and documents posted to Academia Sinica after a successful preliminary evaluation.
english_requirement: Most programmes require English proficiency test scores such as TOEFL, IELTS, GEPT or TOEIC; the EAMW programme requires other language scores. For official score reports, institution name must be Academia Sinica and code 7142.
duration: First-year stipend, extendable for one further year for students who perform well; doctoral study of three years
description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program is a PhD programme supported by Academia Sinica and fifteen partner universities, offering a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for one further year for students who perform well.

not_confirmed: selection_criteria (each TIGP PhD programme sets its own admission criteria)
verification.notes: Stipend and its NT$6,000 tax-free extension, the upgrade for strong students, the tuition subsidy for five consecutive years, the domestic tuition rates, the English proficiency requirement and the application period were all read directly from Academia Sinica's TIGP site. The tuition model is important: this is a subsidy of the international-to-domestic fee difference, not a tuition waiver, so international students still pay the domestic tuition rate of about NT$28,000 to 31,000 per semester for the first four semesters. The monthly stipend is tax-free for the first year and is dependent on the individual thesis advisor thereafter. Results are announced around the middle of March.

applicant_utility: The TIGP stipend is NT$40,000 a month and, unusually, tax-free - but the word 'tax-free' covers the base amount, so check the conditions attached to the NT$34,000 plus NT$6,000 structure on the current application materials. It is guaranteed for your first year and extended for one more year if you perform well, after which the amount depends on your individual thesis advisor, so choose your supervisor with that in mind. The most common misconception is that tuition is free: it is not. Academia Sinica only bridges the gap between international and domestic fees, so you will still pay roughly NT$28,000 to 31,000 per semester for your first four semesters on top of your living costs. You can apply to only one TIGP programme, and you must choose your thesis advisor before the end of your first year. Send transcripts as originals in sealed envelopes straight from your registrar - non-notarised photocopies and screenshots are not accepted - and note that scores are only accepted if you name Academia Sinica, code 7142.
